claim: When tool arguments are strings with minor textual differences despite identical semantics, cache hit rate is low because the serialized arguments create distinct nodes in the tool call graph.
falsifier: Design a tool call cache with exact string matching on serialized arguments and measure hit rate for tools whose arguments are strings with possible textual variation.

conditions: Cache uses exact string matching on serialized tool arguments
Tool arguments are strings that can vary textually while preserving meaning
exclusions: Evidence is limited to object memory querying and visual question answering tools in the video understanding workload

title: String arguments with minor–Low cache hit rate principle

claim: In restrained MD simulations, the effectiveness of restraint selection methods for inducing conformational changes depends on whether they use target structure information: methods using target information (largest change in pairwise separation) yield the lowest RMSD, while methods without target information (normal mode analysis, largest Cα separation) achieve intermediate results, and random selection performs poorly.
falsifier: The ranking can be tested by performing restrained MD simulations on a protein with two known conformations, applying each restraint selection method with the same number of restraints, and comparing the resulting RMSD to the target.

conditions: protein has two distinct conformational states
number of restraints is small (Nr up to 5)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported proteins (T4L, PGK, AK, GB1) and the AMBER99SB-ILDN force field; relative performance may depend on protein.

title: Restraint selection method for effectiveness measured by Cα
